newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan sees little danger from Australia's anthrax.
newsitem.headline: Japan sees little danger from Australia's anthrax.

text.p: Japanese officials and traders said on Friday they are still studying the effects of the anthrax bacterium which was found in some dairy herds in Australia, but said the reaction from importers and consumers have been muted so far.

"We"re collecting the necessary information on anthrax from Australia through diplomatic channels," said an official of the Health and Welfare Ministry. He added that the ministry had no plans to issue any official warnings at the moment.
Japanese trading firms have shown no signs of cutting back dairy imports from Australia so far, said an official from the Australian Dairy Corporation's Tokyo office.
Traders agreed that the outbreak had not raised any fears in Japan.
"The outbreak was limited to Victoria (region of Australia) and we see no risk of consumers contracting the disease through food products," said one livestock trader at Mitsubishi Corp.

"Some trade houses approached us to ask about how they should react (to the anthrax outbreak). But we"ve received no queries from local consumer groups so far," an official of the Agriculture Ministry said.
Anthrax, a bacterial infection, causes rapid death in cattle, sheep and goats. It rarely affects humans but can be contracted through a small cut or scratch.
The Australian government said on Friday that the incidence of anthrax in some its dairy herds posed no health implications for consumers of dairy or other animal products.
It said only people who come in to direct contact with anthrax-affected animals needed to be careful.
Japan imported 49,694 tonnes of cheese and 11,760 tonnes of skimmed milk powder from Australia during the January-November period of 1996, the latest available data.
